title: Narrative Text
summary: Deciphering narrative fiction, folklore, and fables: narrative arc (orientation, complication, climax, resolution), character traits, moral themes, and figurative symbolism.

lessons.title: The Narrative Curve: Complication, Escalation, Climax, and Resolution

blocks.html:
The Anatomy of Storytelling: Freytag's Narrative Pyramid

Narrative Text entertains, enchants, and educates readers by presenting an engaging story involving human or anthropomorphic characters confronting a crisis. The core driving engine of any narrative is the conflict.

blocks.title: Real-World Context: The Universal Rhythm of Storytelling
blocks.html: From Hollywood blockbuster movies to traditional Indonesian folk tales like Malin Kundang and Sangkuriang, every captivating story follows a universal dramatic heartbeat: peace is disrupted, obstacles mount to an unbearable breaking point, a decisive confrontation unfolds, and a new equilibrium is forged. This dynamic trajectory is the Narrative Curve.

blocks.title: Historical Insight: Freytag's Dramatic Pyramid
blocks.html:
Tokoh: Gustav Freytag Tahun: 1863 M Krisis: Readers fail to distinguish the inciting incident (minor obstacle) from the major climax, leading to inaccurate summaries of literary passages.

Nineteenth-century scholar Gustav Freytag mapped narrative arcs in dramatic literature, establishing the canonical stages of Exposition, Inciting Incident, Rising Action, Climax, Falling Action, and Resolution that underpin modern reading assessment design.

blocks.title: Conceptual Definition: The Generic Structure of Narrative Texts
blocks.html: A Narrative Text entertains and engages readers through an imaginative sequence of human or anthropomorphic experiences dealing with problematic complications. Stages: 1. Orientation (Setting & Characters), 2. Complication (The emergence of conflict), 3. Climax (Peak dramatic confrontation), 4. Resolution (Crisis resolved happily or tragically), and 5. Re-orientation / Coda (Moral reflection).

blocks.title: Stages of the English Narrative Genre
blocks.html:
Orientation → Complication → Climax → Resolution
Tahap / KomponenFungsi Retoris / MaknaCiri Kebahasaan / Contoh Penerapan
OrientationEstablishes 'Who', 'Where', 'When', and the baseline atmosphereSetting the scene
ComplicationDisrupts normal equilibrium with an external or internal dilemmaCatalyst for action
ClimaxThe pivotal moment of maximum jeopardy and fateful choiceDramatic turning point
ResolutionThe knot is untied; order is restored or transformation occursDenouement / Outcome
Coda / Moral ValueExplicit or implicit life lesson derived from the ordealThematic takeaway

Pedagogical Note: Narratives are predominantly written in Past Tense with dynamic Action Verbs and Direct Spoken Dialogue.

blocks.title: Simulasi Interaktif: Memetakan Busur Naratif Dongeng & Legenda
blocks.caption: Tentukan titik balik klimaks dan komplikasi cerita rakyat klasik melalui visualisasi interaktif.

blocks.title: Tiga Tipe Konflik Utama
blocks.html:
• Person vs Person: Pertentangan protagonis vs antagonis (misalnya: persaingan dua saudara).
  • Person vs Nature / Society: Pertentangan tokoh melawan bencana alam atau norma sosial yang tidak adil.
  • Person vs Self (Internal Conflict): Pergulatan batin tokoh melawan rasa bersalah, ketakutan, atau godaan moral.

blocks.title: Applied Analytical Scenario: The Narrative Curve: Complication, Escalation, Climax, and Resolution
blocks.question: How can a critical reader analyze and verify discourse arguments regarding 'The Narrative Curve: Complication, Escalation, Climax, and Resolution' based on principles articulated by Gustav Freytag?

steps.step: Identify Textual Claims and Operational Constraints
steps.explanation: Examine the core assertions in the target text and locate the explicit warrants connecting premises to the central thesis of The Narrative Curve: Complication, Escalation, Climax, and Resolution.

steps.step: Evaluate Evidence Quality and Rhetorical Framing
steps.explanation: Cross-examine whether the supporting data meets scholarly standards, checking for potential logical fallacies or biases.

steps.step: Synthesize Authorial Stance and Strategic Implications
steps.explanation: Determine the underlying communicative purpose and synthesize actionable conclusions aligned with Gustav Freytag's framework.

blocks.answer: By systematically evaluating textual evidence and logical structure, readers can resolve complex comprehension challenges regarding The Narrative Curve: Complication, Escalation, Climax, and Resolution with critical confidence.

blocks.title: Comprehension Check: The Narrative Curve: Complication, Escalation, Climax, and Resolution
blocks.question: Which of the following statements most accurately reflects the core principle established by Gustav Freytag regarding 'The Narrative Curve: Complication, Escalation, Climax, and Resolution'?

options.A: The concept relies entirely on subjective guesswork without requiring any textual or empirical justification.
options.B: The principle provides a rigorous analytical framework grounded in verifiable evidence and coherent logical relations.
options.C: The rule is completely obsolete and has been universally rejected by all modern academic institutions.
options.D: The structure can only be applied when reading ancient fictional poetry and is invalid for academic prose.
options.E: The framework mandates that readers must accept all internet claims without checking author credibility.

blocks.explanation: Option B is correct. In academic discourse, The Narrative Curve: Complication, Escalation, Climax, and Resolution establishes systematic criteria for rigorous critical analysis. Option A is incorrect because validity requires evidence. Option C is false as the framework remains foundational. Option D is incorrect because it applies across academic genres. Option E contradicts the principles of critical evaluation.
blocks.hint: Identify the option emphasizing evidence-based reasoning, logical consistency, and scholarly integrity.

lessons.title: Character Traits: Direct vs Indirect Characterization

blocks.html:
Decoding Characters: The STEAL Method of Characterization

In literary narrative reading comprehension, questions rarely ask for simple physical appearance. They ask: 'Which word best describes the king's character?' or 'Why did the merchant betray his companion?'

Authors develop character depth through two approaches:

  1. Direct Characterization: The author explicitly tells the reader what the character is like (e.g., 'Jack was an impatient and arrogant young prince.').
  2. Indirect Characterization: The author reveals character traits subtly through actions, dialogue, thoughts, and reactions.

blocks.title: Real-World Context: Reading People Between the Lines
blocks.html: If a person regularly tells everyone: 'I am the most generous person in this town', but when an elderly beggar approaches they look away and clutch their designer handbag, what is their real character? In literature and life, actions, posture, and subtle gestures reveal far more truth than outward verbal declarations.

blocks.title: Historical Insight: Henry James and The Art of Fiction
blocks.html:
Tokoh: Henry James Tahun: 1884 M Krisis: Readers rely solely on narrator statements, missing subtle traits conveyed through dialogue, body language, and symbolic habits.

Literary master Henry James in The Art of Fiction (1884) famously argued: 'What is character but the determination of incident? What is incident but the illustration of character?' James pioneered psychological realism, showing that characterization should unfold organically through behavioral evidence.

blocks.title: Conceptual Definition: Direct Telling vs Indirect Showing (STEAL Method)
blocks.html: Direct Characterization: The author explicitly tells the reader what a character is like (e.g., 'Jack was impatient and stubborn'). Indirect Characterization: The author shows the character's traits through five dimensions of evidence: Speech, Thoughts, Effect on others, Actions, and Looks (STEAL method).

blocks.title: The STEAL Framework for Literary Trait Analysis
blocks.html:
Speech (Dialogue) → Thoughts (Inner Monologue) → Effect on Others → Actions (Behavior)
Tahap / KomponenFungsi Retoris / MaknaCiri Kebahasaan / Contoh Penerapan
Speech (Dialogue)Tone, accent, choice of vocabulary, sarcasm, hesitant pausesWhat & how they speak
Thoughts (Inner Monologue)Secret anxieties, motivations, ethical dilemmas, hidden jealousiesInterior cognitive plane
Effect on OthersHow secondary characters react around them (fear, reverence, distaste)Social gravitational field
Actions (Behavior)Decisive choices under pressure, involuntary physical ticsEthical manifestations
Looks (Appearance)Dress style, posture, condition of hands, symbolic accessoriesExternalized identity

Pedagogical Note: Test questions testing character traits require quoting specific textual clues matching the STEAL indicators.

blocks.title: Contoh Analisis Karakterisasi Tak Langsung
blocks.question: Passage: 'When the starving wanderer knocked at his manor gate, Lord Roderick instructed his butler to lock the iron latches twice, muttering that beggars brought nothing but fleas. He then retreated to the banquet hall and emptied another goblet of spiced wine.' What trait does Lord Roderick demonstrate?
steps: Aksi (Action): Memerintahkan penguncian gerbang besi dua kali terhadap musafir kelaparan.
Ucapan (Speech): Menyebut pengemis hanya membawa kutu ('beggars brought nothing but fleas').
Gaya Hidup: Kembali minum anggur mahal di ruang perjamuan mewahnya.
Sintesis Sifat: Kikir, berhati dingin, egois, dan tidak memiliki empati (callous, selfish, miserly).
blocks.answer: Lord Roderick adalah sosok yang callous, selfish, and devoid of compassion (berhati dingin dan egois).

blocks.title: Cek Pemahaman
blocks.question: A protagonist donates his last loaf of bread to an elderly beggar despite having not eaten for two days. This action primarily reveals that the protagonist is...
blocks.hint: Altruistic berarti mementingkan keselamatan/kebutuhan orang lain di atas diri sendiri.
blocks.explanation: Tindakan mengorbankan makanan terakhir untuk orang lain menunjukkan sifat altruistik dan penuh welas asih (altruistic and compassionate).

lessons.title: Reading Spoken Dialogue and Indirect Speech Clues

blocks.html:
Subtext in Dialogue: Reading Between the Lines

Characters in sophisticated stories rarely say exactly what they mean. In TKA narrative questions, you must look beyond literal words to decipher subtext, irony, and conversational tension embedded in dialogue tags.

blocks.title: Real-World Context: How Dialogue Reveals Who a Character Really Is
blocks.html: In stories, an author rarely tells you directly: 'Lady Catherine was arrogant and cruel'. Instead, the author shows her speaking in clipped, imperious sentences: '"Do you know who I am? How dare you speak to me in that tone!" she snapped.' Dialogue is a window into a character's hidden psychology, social status, and moral integrity.

blocks.title: Historical Insight: Mikhail Bakhtin and The Dialogic Imagination
blocks.html:
Tokoh: Mikhail Bakhtin Tahun: 1981 M Krisis: Students miss character clues hidden in spoken dialogue and get tripped up by reported speech tense transformations.

Literary theorist Mikhail Bakhtin wrote The Dialogic Imagination (1981). Bakhtin demonstrated that narrative prose achieves its power through polyphony (multiple voices): spoken dialogue reflects the genuine clash of conflicting worldviews and moral values.

blocks.title: Conceptual Definition: Direct Speech vs Indirect (Reported) Speech Clues
blocks.html:
Direct Speech: The exact verbatim words spoken by a character, enclosed in quotation marks and accompanied by expressive reporting verbs and adverbs (e.g., "Run!" he whispered urgently.).

Indirect Speech: The narrator's paraphrase of what was said, undergoing grammatical backshift (e.g., He urged them to run immediately.).

blocks.title: Narrative Dialogue Decoding Matrix
blocks.html:
Isolate Spoken Utterance → Audit Reporting Verb & Adverb → Notice Syntactic Tense Backshift → Deduce Character Trait & Emotional State
Tahap / KomponenFungsi Retoris / MaknaCiri Kebahasaan / Contoh Penerapan
Expressive Reporting VerbsReplaces bland 'said' with verbs revealing emotional tone'Murmured' (secrecy), 'bellowed' (fury), 'stammered' (nervousness), 'sneered' (contempt)
Grammatical BackshiftPresent tense in direct speech shifts to past tense in reported speech'I know the secret' → 'He claimed that he knew the secret.'
Subtext and IronyWhen a character's spoken words contradict their physical actions'"I am completely calm," she said, her hands trembling uncontrollably.'
Pronoun TransformationsShifting deictic markers from speaker's perspective to third-person'"This is my home"' → 'She declared that that was her home.'

Pedagogical Note: In narrative reading questions, pay close attention to reporting verbs and descriptive manner adverbs to deduce a character's true underlying motive.

blocks.title: Contoh Analisis Subteks Dialog
blocks.question: Excerpt: '"Of course your navigation skills are unmatched," Cedric sneered, glancing toward their stranded cart stuck axle-deep in the swamp mud.' What does Cedric actually mean?
steps: Kalimat harfiah: 'Tentu saja kemampuan navigasimu tak tertandingi.'
Konteks situasi nyata: Gerobak mereka terperosok sedalam poros roda di dalam lumpur rawa akibat salah jalan.
Makna sebenarnya (Verbal Irony): Cedric sedang mengejek dan menyalahkan navigasi rekannya yang sangat buruk sehingga membuat mereka terjebak.
blocks.answer: Cedric bermaksud menyindir dan mengkritik pedas kesalahan arah rekan perjalanannya.

blocks.title: Cek Pemahaman
blocks.question: If a character says: '"I suppose you might be right after all," she conceded, looking away,' the word conceded indicates that she...

options.C: reluctantly admitted the validity of the other person's point.

blocks.hint: Concede berarti mengakui kebenaran pihak lain secara enggan/berat hati.
blocks.explanation: 'Conceded' berarti mengakui atau mengalah secara enggan terhadap argumen orang lain.

lessons.title: Uncovering Moral Lessons, Themes, and Allegorical Wisdom

blocks.html:
Deriving Universal Themes from Folklore and Fables

Every traditional fable, folklore, and myth conveys a moral value or universal theme. In TKA reading items, questions such as 'What moral lesson can be derived from the story?' require you to generalize the specific conflict into an enduring principle of human conduct.

blocks.title: Real-World Context: Why Animal Stories Rule Human Literature
blocks.html: In George Orwell's Animal Farm, pigs take over a farm and walk on two legs. Is Orwell writing a book on agriculture and animal husbandry? Of course not! The animals are an Allegory: a powerful literary mirror reflecting human greed, totalitarian corruption, and the betrayal of political ideals. Stories carry timeless moral and philosophical wisdom wrapped in imaginative vessels.

blocks.title: Historical Insight: Northrop Frye and Archetypal Literary Theory
blocks.html:
Tokoh: Aesop & Northrop Frye Tahun: 1957 M Krisis: Readers treat a classic animal fable as merely a cute children's story, failing to extract the profound universal allegorical critique of human political behavior.

Canadian literary theorist Northrop Frye in Anatomy of Criticism (1957) mapped the archetypal patterns of myth and fable, showing that allegories transmit enduring ethical principles across cultural generations.

blocks.title: Conceptual Definition: Theme vs Topic vs Moral Lesson
blocks.html:
1. Topic: The subject matter in one or two words (e.g., 'Courage', 'Greed').
2. Theme: The author's central philosophical statement about life or human nature (e.g., 'Unchecked greed ultimately destroys the very prosperity it seeks to hoard').
3. Moral Lesson: The prescriptive ethical guidance offered to the reader (e.g., 'We should practice gratitude and moderation rather than endless avarice').
4. Allegory: An extended metaphor where characters and events symbolize deeper political, moral, or spiritual realities.

blocks.title: Formulating Universal Thematic Statements
blocks.html:
Avoid Raw Topics → Avoid Plot Summaries → Universal Human Statement
Tahap / KomponenFungsi Retoris / MaknaCiri Kebahasaan / Contoh Penerapan
Avoid Raw Topics'The story is about animals' -> WRONG (Merely a superficial topic)Too shallow
Avoid Plot Summaries'The story shows that Jack climbed the beanstalk' -> WRONG (Merely a plot event)Too specific
Universal Human Statement'True resourcefulness and humility triumph over arrogant brute strength' -> CORRECT (Universal theme)True philosophical theme

Pedagogical Note: On TKA moral questions: Look for universal philosophical truths applicable to human life broadly, not just statements about story characters.

blocks.title: Contoh Perumusan Nilai Moral TKA
blocks.question: Which statement best captures the moral of a story where a king trades his daughter's freedom for a pile of glittering jewels, only to die lonely in an empty palace?
steps: Opsi A: Gold and jewels are the safest assets during times of political instability.
Opsi B: Material wealth cannot replace the irreplaceable bond of family and human warmth.
Opsi C: Kings should hire more guards to protect their castle treasuries.
Opsi D: Daughters should always obey their father's royal decrees.
blocks.answer: Pilihan B adalah simpulan moral universal yang tepat. Pilihan A, C, dan D gagal menangkap pesan filosofis tentang kehampaan kekayaan materi.

blocks.title: Cek Pemahaman
blocks.question: What is a defining characteristic of a properly formulated moral lesson in a TKA exam?

options.A: It must mention the specific names of the animal characters.
options.B: It is expressed as a broad, universal truth applicable to real-world human behavior.
options.C: It must always rhyme like a nursery proverb.
options.D: It is always stated verbatim in the opening sentence of the orientation.

blocks.explanation: Pesan moral dirumuskan sebagai kebenaran universal yang berlaku luas bagi perilaku manusia di dunia nyata, tanpa terbatas pada nama tokoh fiksi.

lessons.title: Predicting Outcomes: Foreshadowing, Irony, and Plot Twists

blocks.html:
Literary Mechanics: Foreshadowing and Situational Irony

Authors plant subtle clues early in the narrative to prepare readers for what will happen later—a device known as foreshadowing. When the eventual outcome sharply contradicts what characters and readers reasonably anticipated, it is called situational irony.

blocks.title: Real-World Context: The Shock That Makes Perfect Retrospective Sense
blocks.html: In O. Henry's immortal short story The Gift of the Magi, a wife cuts and sells her long beautiful hair to buy a platinum chain for her husband's pocket watch, while the husband sells his pocket watch to buy luxurious tortoise-shell combs for her hair! A brilliant plot twist never violates narrative logic; it shocks the reader initially, but instantly feels satisfying and inevitable in retrospect.

blocks.title: Historical Insight: O. Henry and the Poetics of Situational Irony
blocks.html:
Tokoh: O. Henry & Anton Chekhov Tahun: 1905 M Krisis: Readers perceive plot twists as illogical accidents rather than recognizing the subtle irony and narrative breadcrumbs planted earlier.

American master of the short story O. Henry (William Sydney Porter, 1905) perfected the art of Situational Irony: a sharp disparity between expected outcomes and actual reality that produces profound empathy and humor.

blocks.title: Conceptual Definition: Three Varieties of Literary Irony
blocks.html:
1. Situational Irony: When actions produce an effect that is the exact opposite of what was intended by the characters.
2. Dramatic Irony: When the audience/reader possesses crucial knowledge that the story characters remain blissfully unaware of.
3. Verbal Irony: When a character says one thing while intending the opposite (sarcasm / subtle mockery).

blocks.title: Dissecting Foreshadowing and Outcome Clues
blocks.html:
Ominous Weather / Setting → Symbolic Micro-Incidents → Unheeded Warnings
Tahap / KomponenFungsi Retoris / MaknaCiri Kebahasaan / Contoh Penerapan
Ominous Weather / SettingSudden darkening skies, violent thunder claps, flickering streetlampsPrelude to conflict
Symbolic Micro-IncidentsA cracked porcelain vase, a dead bird on the porch, a stopped pocket watchHarbingers of disruption
Unheeded WarningsA wise elder's ignored advice, an ominous inscription on an ancient doorwayIrony catalyst

Pedagogical Note: When predicting story outcomes in exams: Choose the option that resolves the central foreshadowed conflict logically.

blocks.title: Mendeteksi Petunjuk Foreshadowing
blocks.html: Perhatikan detail kecil yang tampaknya sepele di paragraf awal: cuaca yang tiba-tiba bergemuruh, peringatan penjaga tua yang diabaikan, atau benda kecil yang disimpan ke dalam saku. Detail tersebut hampir pasti menjadi kunci penyelamat atau malapetaka di klimaks cerita!

blocks.title: Contoh Analisis Foreshadowing
blocks.question: Early paragraph: 'As Arthur strapped on his grandfather’s tarnished breastplate, he noticed a hairline fracture near the central clasp, but dismissed it in his hurry to join the tournament.' What outcome does this detail foreshadow?
steps: Detail awal: retakan rambut (hairline fracture) pada pelat dada zirah.
Tindakan tokoh: mengabaikannya karena terburu-buru ('dismissed it in his hurry').
Prediksi logis berbasis foreshadowing: Saat turnamen berlangsung, zirah tersebut kemungkinan besar akan pecah tepat di bagian retakan tersebut ketika dihantam tombak lawan.
blocks.answer: Detail retakan zirah memberikan petunjuk awal bahwa zirah akan hancur dan membahayakan keselamatan Arthur saat bertarung.

blocks.title: Cek Pemahaman
blocks.question: In a suspenseful short story, the sudden malfunction of a vehicle's headlights just before the protagonist enters a desolate mountain pass is a classic example of...
blocks.hint: Lampu mobil yang mati sebelum memasuki jalan pegunungan adalah firasat bahaya.
blocks.explanation: Kerusakan lampu mobil di tempat terpencil adalah perangkat sastra 'foreshadowing' yang menandakan bahaya besar akan menghadang di depan.

lessons.title: Distraktor Jebakan: Fakta Dunia Nyata vs Logika Fiksi

blocks.html:
The Golden Rule of Narrative Comprehension: Honor the Story's Reality

In stories featuring folklore, magical realism, or mythical creatures, real-world biological laws do not apply. If a fable states that 'The dragon’s scales turned into impenetrable emerald glass whenever tears touched them,' you must treat that statement as an absolute truth within the narrative framework.

blocks.title: Real-World Context: Can a Wooden Puppet's Nose Really Grow?
blocks.html: In the real world, human noses do not grow longer when telling lies. But inside the magical universe of Pinocchio, a growing nose is an absolute physical truth! One of the most common pitfalls in literature reading assessments is bringing outside real-world science or modern legal logic into a fictional universe that operates under its own internal rules.

blocks.title: Historical Insight: Coleridge and 'Willing Suspension of Disbelief'
blocks.html:
Tokoh: Samuel Taylor Coleridge Tahun: 1817 M Krisis: Test-takers select answers based on real-world biology or modern laws rather than the established internal rules of the fairy tale or fantasy passage.

English romantic poet and philosopher Samuel Taylor Coleridge coined the foundational concept in Biographia Literaria (1817): the 'willing suspension of disbelief'—the tacit agreement by the reader to accept the fictional parameters established by the storyteller.

blocks.title: Conceptual Definition: Intra-Diegetic Logic vs Real-World Distractors
blocks.html: Intra-Diegetic Logic refers to the internal laws, magical mechanics, moral codes, and premise rules established within the world of the story. In reading tests, examiners construct tempting distractors that are scientifically accurate in the real world (e.g., 'Dragons cannot breathe fire because organic lungs cannot produce combustion') but completely FALSE within the narrative text universe.

blocks.title: Mitigating Real-World Distractor Traps in Fiction Tests
blocks.html:
Rule 1: Text Supremacy → Rule 2: Motive Alignment → Rule 3: Reject Outside Trivia
Tahap / KomponenFungsi Retoris / MaknaCiri Kebahasaan / Contoh Penerapan
Rule 1: Text SupremacyThe passage's internal reality overrides external real-world scientific lawsHonor fictional premises
Rule 2: Motive AlignmentJudge character choices by their fictional worldview, not 21st-century valuesHistorical & moral context
Rule 3: Reject Outside TriviaIf an option relies on external facts absent from the passage, eliminate it immediatelyText-boundary discipline

Pedagogical Note: Never argue with the passage using external science facts; answer exclusively from the narrative's internal universe.

blocks.title: Jebakan Logika Ilmiah Dunia Nyata pada Teks Sastra
blocks.html: Pilihan distraktor sering menyodorkan penjelasan sains modern yang masuk akal di dunia nyata (misalnya: 'Reptiles cannot breathe fire due to lack of combustible glands') untuk menolak peristiwa fiksi. Pilihlah selalu jawaban berdasarkan hukum logika cerita fiksi tersebut!

blocks.title: Contoh Analisis Batas Fiksi
blocks.question: Story: 'By whispering the sacred verse, the princess caused the barren cherry tree to bloom instantaneously with golden blossoms in the dead of winter.' Question: Why did the cherry tree bloom? (A) Due to unseasonably warm temperatures and soil nutrients. (B) Because the princess uttered the sacred incantation.
steps: Evaluasi (A): Penjelasan ilmiah dunia nyata, tetapi bertentangan langsung dengan teks yang menyatakan pohon mekar 'in the dead of winter'.
Evaluasi (B): Sesuai dengan logika magis cerita: 'By whispering the sacred verse'.
blocks.answer: Jawaban benar adalah (B). Jangan terjebak penjelasan sains dunia nyata yang tidak ada di teks fiksi.

blocks.title: Cek Pemahaman
blocks.question: When answering reading comprehension questions about a myth or fantasy tale, what is your primary source of truth?

options.A: Modern scientific textbooks and biological laws.
options.B: Common sense principles of everyday physics.
options.C: The internal rules and explicit events established within the text stimulus.

blocks.hint: Kebenaran mutlak bersumber murni dari teks stimulus.
blocks.explanation: Segala simpulan dan jawaban wajib didasarkan secara murni pada aturan internal dan peristiwa yang tertulis di dalam teks stimulus.

lessons.title: Comprehensive Narrative Reading Practice and Quiz

blocks.html:
Narrative Mastery Exam Review

Put your literary analysis skills to the test. Before beginning, remember:

  • Trace the complication: what specific inciting event disrupted peace?
  • Assess character traits through actions and subtext, not superficial words.
  • Formulate moral themes as universal truths about life and ethics.

blocks.title: Simulasi Soal Cerita
blocks.html: Kuis ini terdiri atas 20 butir soal standar TKA yang mencakup fabel klasik, legenda nusantara berbahasa Inggris, dan cerpen fiksi kontemporer.

blocks.title: Cheat Sheet: Narrative Text, Plot & Moral Values
blocks.subtitle: Summary of orientation, complication, resolution, coda, character motivation, and theme analysis.
blocks.html:
1. Narrative Plot Trajectory

  1. Orientation: Introduction of characters, setting, and temporal context.
  2. Complication: The inciting incident triggers a rising crisis or dilemma for the protagonist.
  3. Climax: The peak of emotional intensity or highest conflict.
  4. Resolution: The crisis is resolved (happily or tragically).
  5. Coda / Moral Value: The underlying ethical lesson conveyed to the audience.

2. Conflict Categories

  • Internal (Man vs Self): Moral dilemmas, guilt, fear, difficult choices.
  • External: Man vs Man (antagonist), Man vs Nature (survival), Man vs Society (unjust laws).

blocks.text: Kuis Uji Kompetensi TKA Bahasa Inggris: Narrative Text (20 Soal Pilihan Ganda Terstandar).
